title: Jesse Eisenberg Says Fans Aren’t Crazy With Him Because ‘There’s No Sexuality to My Work’: Life Is ‘Different’ When People ‘Want to Sleep With’ You
content:
ByPayton Turkeltaub

Jesse Eisenbergrecently told theNew Yorkerthat fans of his are “mostly fine” when he’s in public, a fact he attributes to his generally sexless resume.

“People are mostly fine,” he said to reporter Rachel Syme when asked if strangers ever interrupt him when they spot him working on scripts. (The “A Real Pain” actor told Syme that his typical schedule revolves around sitting at a branch of the New York Public Library, where he writes from nine to five). “It’s because there’s no sexuality to my work,” he continued. “I think once the public is asked to want to sleep with a person onscreen, that person’s life is fundamentally different.”

Though, despite Eisenberg’s assertion, his “Fleishman Is in Trouble” co-starClaire Danestold Syme that people began to “rubberneck” when the two had a coincidental run-in on the street and stopped to chat. “People are very aware of him as a figure, even though he is so determined to be invisible,” she said.

Elsewhere in the lengthy profile, Aaron Sorkin, who directed Eisenberg as a young Mark Zuckerberg in “The Social Network,” told the outlet that “I hardly know him at all,” noting that the actor reminds “me of Holden Caulfield, if that makes any sense. He has absolutely no patience for phonies.”

Eisenberg earned an Oscar nomination for the part, but has since been outspoken about hisdecision not to reprise the rolein the director’s follow-up, “The Social Reckoning,” released earlier this year. “I’d be out at a bar, and a drunk guy would say, ‘Hey, I love your website,’” he told the New Yorker. “And as I’m pretending to laugh, I’d just wish all of the oxygen would leave my lungs, and that I would collapse on the floor in front of this guy and show him what he’s doing to me.”

The actor-turned-director, who is currently promoting “The Debut,” his latest project, also spoke about creating “nonhierarchical” environments on his sets. “How could you be making a movie about a woman who’s an underdog, who no one notices, and then have a set where the people walking around feel like that?” he said. “You’d have to be so stupid and blind and compartmentalizing, in a psychopathic way, to write a movie about that and then perpetuate it.”

“The Debut,” Eisenberg’s third feature as a director, starsJulianne Mooreas Mona Friedman, a New Jersey housewife who auditions for a part in her local theater’s production of a fictional musical. After she’s cast as Miss Danielle, Friedman’s life begins to unravel as she becomes more consumed with the role and falls under the spell of director Jerry Blankenbuehler (Paul Giamatti).

“The Debut” opens from A24 in theaters on Dec. 11
title_zh: 傑西·艾森伯格(Jesse Eisenberg)表示，粉絲對他的熱情並不瘋狂，因為「我的作品中沒有性吸引力」：當人們「想和你上床」時，生活會變得「不同」。
content_zh:
由佩頓·圖克塔布(Payton Turkeltaub)報導

傑西·艾森伯格(Jesse Eisenberg)最近在《紐約客》(The New Yorker)中表示，他的粉絲在公共場合“通常都很好”，他將這一事實歸因於他一般缺乏性暗示的履歷。

“人們通常都很好，”他在接受記者瑞秋·西姆(Rachel Syme)的詢問時說，當時她問他是否有陌生人在他工作寫劇本時打擾他。（這位《真正的痛苦》(A Real Pain)演員告訴西姆，他的日常安排通常是在紐約公共圖書館的一個分館裡，從早上九點寫到下午五點。） “這是因為我的作品沒有性暗示，”他接著說。“我認為一旦公眾被要求想要和銀幕上的某個人發生關係，那個人的生活就會根本不同。”

儘管艾森伯格的說法如此，他在《弗萊許曼有麻煩》(Fleishman Is in Trouble)中的搭檔克萊爾·丹斯(Claire Danes)告訴西姆，當他們在街上偶然相遇並停下來聊天時，人們開始“圍觀”。“人們非常清楚他作為一個人物，即使他如此努力地想要隱形，”她說。

在這篇長篇專訪中，亞倫·索金(Aaron Sorkin)談到他曾在《社交網路》(The Social Network)中導演年輕的馬克·祖克伯格(Jesse Eisenberg)，並告訴媒體：“我幾乎對他一無所知，”並指出這位演員讓他想起“霍爾登·考爾菲德(Holden Caulfield)，如果這樣說有意義的話。他對虛偽的人完全沒有耐心。”

艾森伯格因該角色獲得奧斯卡提名，但自此以來，他對於不重返導演的續集《社交清算》(The Social Reckoning)的決定表達了強烈的看法，該片於今年早些時候上映。“我在酒吧裡，醉漢會說，‘嘿，我喜歡你的網站，’”他告訴《紐約客》。 “當我假裝笑的時候，我只希望所有的氧氣都離開我的肺，我會在這個人面前倒下，讓他看到他對我造成了什麼。”

這位轉型為導演的演員，目前正在推廣他的最新作品《首演》(The Debut)，他也談到了在拍攝現場創造“非階層化”環境的想法。“你怎麼能拍一部關於一個被忽視的弱者女性的電影，然後在拍攝現場讓走來走去的人感覺到這一點呢？”他說。“你必須是如此愚蠢、盲目和分隔思維，以一種精神病的方式，才能寫出這樣的電影然後又延續它。”

《首演》是艾森伯格的第三部導演作品，主演是朱莉安·摩爾(Julianne Moore)，她飾演新澤西州的家庭主婦莫娜·弗里德曼(Mona Friedman)，她為當地劇院的一部虛構音樂劇試鏡。當她被選為丹妮爾小姐(Miss Danielle)後，弗里德曼的生活開始崩潰，因為她越來越沉迷於這個角色，並受到導演傑瑞·布蘭肯比勒(Paul Giamatti)的魅力所吸引。

《首演》將於12月11日由A24在電影院上映。
